partnershipPlan: Two patient partners and two night nurses review the round's wording to patients and the waking question; the night bank manager joins the fortnightly huddle once a month.
socialListening: No social media listening; the wards' patient comment cards are read for mentions of night-time care.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (night nurse): When there are nine of them and one of me, turning is the job I promise myself I will do after the drugs round.
items.implication: Protect the round at fixed times rather than asking nurses to fit it in.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I would rather be turned than get a sore, but tell me before you do it.
items.implication: Explain the round at the evening handover and ask about waking preferences.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Nobody saw it until it was an open wound, and my father's skin never looks red.
items.implication: Touch-based assessment and reporting by skin tone.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (ward manager): Every injury form reads like it is somebody's fault, and the night staff stop reporting.
items.implication: Ward-level reporting only and inspection-based measurement.

summary: Four composite voices on slipping tasks, waking, late detection and blame.
